thread:
sara: Heads-up — customer jane@acme reporting streaming cut-off in Safari (16.4/16.5) connecting to /v1/stream through CDN. It truncates mid-stream (usually ~5–10s), client keeps reconnecting. They see a 304 from CDN then no new chunks. Assigning @josh @mina @kai :thinking:

jane (customer): repro steps (minimal):
1) Open Safari 16.5 on Mac
2) navigator.onLine = true; new EventSource('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc')
3) receive first few events, then connection stalls/hangs, then EventSource fires onerror and reconnects repeatedly. HAR attached in thread below.

josh (frontend): thanks. can you paste the raw response headers and any console output? also which CDN (fastly/cf)?

jane (customer): fastly in front. HEADERS snippet from last successful then-failed attempt:
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 12:02:45 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
X-Cache: HIT
Cache-Control: max-age=3600
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Age: 1234
```
console: "EventSource connection stalled, no message frames"

mina (eng-runtime): 304 is suspicious — SSE should be uncacheable. If CDN serves 304 for `/v1/stream` that implies it cached the preflight or previous response. Do we strip Authorization from cache keys? fastly might return 304 if it thinks resource unchanged and then not stream new chunks.

kai (edge): checking fastly config — we have a caching rule that mistakenly treats OPTIONS/stream endpoints as cacheable when response has Cache-Control set. Looks like origin sometimes returns Cache-Control: max-age=3600 due to a misconfigured middleware when token rotation happens (auth middleware returned an empty body with 200/304 internal). We also see a header `X-Origin-Auth-Status: rotated` in some traces.

ops-bot: Traces: https://observability.redwood/example/trace/afa3f2 — shows connection timeline and three 304s from CDN then no chunked frames forwarded to client.

josh (frontend): Safari's EventSource is picky: if it receives a 304 or an empty 200 mid-stream the browser won't always resume the streaming parser. Polyfills sometimes try to patch by re-opening and replaying but that increases token & connection churn.

jane (customer): HAR attached: https://files.customer/acme-har-0001.har — included. Also seeing intermittent 401s right before some of these 304s (token rotated), so client sees auth errors then 304.

mina (eng-runtime): reproduction idea: run a curl with keepalive and show chunking behavior. Example I want you to run from a mac endpoint and paste output:
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc"
```
Look for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and continuous `data:` lines. If we see 304 then origin likely responded with empty body and fastly returned stale 304.

kai (edge): immediate find: our Fastly VCL had `cacheable_if_no_auth` rule which accidentally matched `/v1/stream` when headers had `X-Origin-Auth-Status: rotated` and we fell back to cached object. That explains 304 hits. Fix is to add explicit `if (req.url.path ~ "^/v1/stream") { pass; }` and ensure preflight OPTIONS never cached.

lucas (billing): note — customer reports elevated token usage because their client reconnects 8–10x. If we patch quickly we can offer a one-time credit. I'll approve a credit if we confirm root cause and timeline.

josh (frontend): quick mitigation we can recommend to customer: set `EventSource` polyfill with exponential backoff and detect Safari userAgent to avoid aggressive reconnects; also ensure no service worker intercepts the stream (SW can double-cache). Can they disable SW for a quick repro?

jane (customer): yes we can test disabling SW. we turned off SW and behavior improved but still saw occasional stalls after a token rotation.

mina (eng-runtime): long-term fix: ensure origin sets `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` on SSE endpoints and add `Vary: Authorization` to prevent CDN reusing cached 304s when auth changes. Short-term edge rule to passthrough `/v1/stream` for 24h. I'll open a patch PR to origin to explicitly set no-store on stream routes.

kai (edge): deploying fastly change to passthrough now to 2 POPs for canary. I'll monitor metrics. ops-bot will post updated trace when canary completes.

ops-bot: Canary deploy started — POPs: ia-fra, us-west. Link: https://deploys.redwood/canary/9876

josh (frontend): also adding additional server-side keepalive ping every 3s (an SSE comment frame) during the session to prevent intermediate proxies from marking this connection idle. This should reduce chance of 304/stall mid-stream.

mina (eng-runtime): created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1448 — origin header fix + tests for `Cache-Control` on SSE endpoints. I added unit test to ensure `Cache-Control` is `no-store`.

jane (customer): testing now with SW disabled and reported edge canary — initial result: much better, only one reconnect after token rotate, no permanent hang. Will run more load tests. Thanks team.

lucas (billing): I'll queue a one-time usage credit while you finish validation.

sara (support): summary/action items: 1) kai/edge applied passthrough canary, monitor (in progress) 2) mina to push origin header fix + tests (PR opened) 3) josh to ship keepalive ping tweak and advise customer polyfill/backoff 4) lucas to provision credit. Reopen if we see further failures. Thanks all :thumbsup:
